title: Taita Sweet Potato Stew
localName: Mchuzi wa Viazi Vitamu wa Taita
author: Mama Wanjiru

heritage.origin: Taita-Taveta County — the Taita Hills of coastal Kenya
heritage.history: The Taita people inhabit the Taita Hills, a mountainous region rising dramatically from the coastal plain near Voi. They are known for their agricultural skill on fertile hillsides where they grow sweet potatoes, sorghum, and beans. The Taita Hills have been inhabited for millennia and the community has developed a unique food culture shaped by both coastal proximity and highland environment.
heritage.modernEvolution: Taita cuisine remains underrepresented in broader Kenyan food culture — this dish is an important record of a rich indigenous tradition.

desc: Taita Sweet Potato Stew — a thick, nourishing stew of sweet potatoes, beans, and seasonal vegetables simmered with onions, tomatoes, and local spices. The traditional cooking of the Taita Hills people.
longDesc: The Taita Hills produce some of Kenya's finest sweet potatoes in their fertile volcanic soil. This traditional stew combines them with beans and whatever vegetables are available, creating a hearty, naturally sweet, deeply satisfying dish.
ingredients: 500g orange-fleshed sweet potatoes — peeled and cubed
1 cup cooked beans — red kidney or black-eyed
1 cup seasonal greens — spinach, kale, or pumpkin leaves
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until soft — 5 minutes.
Add garlic and tomatoes. Cook for 6 minutes until thick.
Add sweet potatoes and water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat. Simmer for 20—25 minutes until sweet potatoes are tender.
Add cooked beans and greens. Stir gently.
Simmer 5 more minutes. Season and garnish with coriander.
chefTips: The sweet potato disintegrates slightly during cooking, naturally thickening the stew.
Add greens only at the end.
cookingScience: Sweet potato starch gelatinises during cooking and some dissolves into the broth, naturally thickening the stew.
sustainabilityTips: Sweet potatoes and beans are nitrogen-fixing crops — particularly sustainable.
culturalNote: The Taita people of the Taita Hills represent one of Kenya's most distinct cultural groups whose mountainous home has produced a unique agricultural and culinary tradition.
